93846.subject: Technical Drawing
93846.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
93846.explanation: The compass is a drawing instrument used to draw circles and arcs of different sizes. It consists of two legs, one with a pointed end and the other with a pencil or pen attachment.

93847.subject: Technical Drawing
93847.question_text: What is the standard size of an A3 drawing sheet in millimeters?
93847.explanation: The standard size of an A3 drawing sheet is 297 mm × 420 mm, following the ISO 216 standard for paper sizes.

93848.subject: Technical Drawing
93848.question_text: Which line type is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
93848.explanation: A dashed line (or hidden line) is used to represent edges or details that are not visible in the current view of an orthographic projection.

93849.subject: Technical Drawing
93849.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
93849.explanation: Drawing a line parallel to one of the arms of the angle is not a step in bisecting an angle. The correct steps involve drawing arcs from the vertex and intersecting points to locate the bisector.

options.text: Drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect both arms
Drawing a line parallel to one of the arms
Drawing arcs from the intersection points to locate the bisector
Joining the vertex to the intersection of the arcs

93850.subject: Technical Drawing
93850.question_text: What is the minimum number of sides required to construct a regular polygon using a compass and straightedge?
93850.explanation: The minimum number of sides for a regular polygon that can be constructed with a compass and straightedge is 3 (an equilateral triangle).

93851.subject: Technical Drawing
93851.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, where is the front view located relative to the plan?
93851.explanation: In first-angle projection, the front view is located above the plan view on the drawing sheet.

options.text: To the right of the plan
To the left of the plan

93852.subject: Technical Drawing
93852.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting it along two intersecting planes?
93852.explanation: A half section is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting it along two intersecting planes, typically removing one-quarter of the object.

93853.subject: Technical Drawing
93853.question_text: In an isometric drawing, what is the angle between the isometric axes?
93853.explanation: In an isometric drawing, the angle between the isometric axes is 120°. This ensures equal foreshortening along all three axes.

93854.subject: Technical Drawing
93854.question_text: Which of the following is not a principle of dimensioning in technical drawing?
93854.explanation: Dimensioning should not be duplicated. Each dimension should be given only once to avoid confusion and errors in interpretation.

options.text: Dimensions should be placed outside the views
Dimensions should be duplicated for clarity
Dimensions should be aligned and grouped
Dimensions should be read from the bottom or right side

93855.subject: Technical Drawing
93855.question_text: Which of the following fasteners is used to prevent relative motion between two rotating parts?
93855.explanation: A key is a mechanical fastener used to prevent relative motion between two rotating parts, such as a shaft and a hub.

40565.subject: Technical Drawing
40565.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
40565.explanation: The compass is the primary tool used in technical drawing to construct circles and arcs of different sizes. It consists of two legs: one with a pointed end for anchoring and the other with a pencil or pen for drawing.

40566.subject: Technical Drawing
40566.question_text: What is the dimension of an A3 drawing sheet in millimeters?
40566.explanation: The A3 sheet size is part of the ISO 216 standard, which defines paper sizes. An A3 sheet measures 297 mm × 420 mm, derived from halving the longer side of an A2 sheet.

40567.subject: Technical Drawing
40567.question_text: Which line type is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
40567.explanation: A dashed line (also called a hidden line) is used in technical drawings to indicate edges or features that are not visible in the current view but exist in the object.

40568.subject: Technical Drawing
40568.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
40568.explanation: Bisecting an angle requires drawing arcs from the vertex and intersecting points, then connecting the vertex to the intersection. Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex is not part of the standard procedure.

options.text: Drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect the angle arms
Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex
Drawing arcs from the intersection points to find the bisector
Connecting the vertex to the intersection of the arcs

40569.subject: Technical Drawing
40569.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the front view is placed:
40569.explanation: In first-angle projection, the front view is placed above the plan (top view), and the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view. This is the standard used in many regions, including Ghana.

options.text: To the right of the side view
To the left of the side view

40570.subject: Technical Drawing
40570.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by removing one-quarter of it?
40570.explanation: A half-section view is used for symmetrical objects, where one-quarter of the object is removed to reveal interior details while retaining half of the exterior view.

40571.subject: Technical Drawing
40571.question_text: In an isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
40571.explanation: In isometric projection, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are equally spaced at 120° to each other, creating a uniform 3D representation.

40572.subject: Technical Drawing
40572.question_text: Which of the following is not a correct dimensioning practice?
40572.explanation: Correct dimensioning practices avoid dimensioning to hidden lines, as this can lead to ambiguity. Dimensions should always refer to visible features.

options.text: Using extension lines to avoid crowding
Placing dimensions outside the view where possible

40573.subject: Technical Drawing
40573.question_text: A drawing is scaled at 1:5. If a line measures 50 mm on the drawing, what is its actual length?
40573.explanation: A scale of 1:5 means the drawing is 5 times smaller than the actual object. To find the actual length, multiply the drawing measurement by the scale factor: 50 mm × 5 = 250 mm.

40574.subject: Technical Drawing
40574.question_text: Which of the following is not typically included in a working drawing?
40574.explanation: A working drawing provides all necessary details for manufacturing or construction, including dimensions, tolerances, and materials. Artistic sketches are not part of working drawings, as they focus on technical accuracy rather than aesthetics.

20065.subject: Technical Drawing
20065.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
20065.explanation: The compass is a drawing tool specifically designed to draw circles and arcs of different sizes by adjusting the distance between its legs. Other tools like the T-square, set square, and protractor serve different purposes.

20066.subject: Technical Drawing
20066.question_text: What is the dimensions of an A2 drawing sheet in millimetres?
20066.explanation: The A2 sheet size is part of the ISO 216 standard, with dimensions of 420 mm × 594 mm. This is derived by halving the longer side of an A1 sheet (594 mm × 841 mm).

20067.subject: Technical Drawing
20067.question_text: Which type of line is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
20067.explanation: A dashed line (also called a hidden line) is used to represent edges or features that are not visible in the current view but exist in the object. Continuous thick lines represent visible outlines, while chain lines are used for center lines.

20068.subject: Technical Drawing
20068.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
20068.explanation: Bisecting an angle requires drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect the angle arms, then drawing intersecting arcs from those points. Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex is not part of the standard bisection procedure.

options.text: Drawing an arc from the vertex to intersect the angle arms
Drawing intersecting arcs from the points where the first arc meets the angle arms
Drawing a perpendicular line from the vertex
Joining the vertex to the intersection of the arcs

20069.subject: Technical Drawing
20069.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the right-side view is placed to the left of which view?
20069.explanation: In first-angle projection, the right-side view is positioned to the left of the front view. This is a key distinction from third-angle projection, where the right-side view is placed to the right of the front view.

20070.subject: Technical Drawing
20070.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by cutting through only half of it?
20070.explanation: A half section is used for symmetrical objects, where only half of the object is sectioned to reveal interior details while the other half remains intact to show external features. Full sections cut through the entire object.

20071.subject: Technical Drawing
20071.question_text: In an isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
20071.explanation: In isometric projection, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are equally spaced at 120° to each other. This creates a 3D representation where all dimensions are drawn to the same scale.

20072.subject: Technical Drawing
20072.question_text: Which of the following shapes cannot be developed into a flat surface without distortion?
20072.explanation: A sphere is a double-curved surface and cannot be developed into a flat plane without distortion. Prisms, cylinders, and pyramids are developable surfaces because they are single-curved or flat.

20073.subject: Technical Drawing
20073.question_text: Which of the following is not a correct dimensioning practice in technical drawing?
20073.explanation: Dimensioning directly on hidden lines is incorrect because dimensions should be placed on visible outlines for clarity. Correct practices include avoiding duplicate dimensions, placing dimensions outside the object, and using extension lines.

options.text: Using extension lines to avoid crowding

20074.subject: Technical Drawing
20074.question_text: In CAD software, which command is used to create a circular array of objects around a central point?
20074.explanation: The ARRAYPOLAR command in CAD software is used to create a circular (polar) array of objects around a specified center point. Other commands like ARRAYRECT create rectangular arrays, while COPY and MOVE do not create arrays.

83745.subject: Technical Drawing
83745.question_text: Which of the following drawing tools is used to draw circles and arcs of varying radii?
83745.explanation: The compass is a drawing instrument used to draw circles and arcs of different sizes. It consists of two legs, one with a pointed end and the other with a pencil or pen attachment.

83746.subject: Technical Drawing
83746.question_text: What is the dimensions of an A3 drawing sheet in millimeters?
83746.explanation: The A3 sheet size is part of the ISO 216 standard and measures 297 mm × 420 mm. Each A-series sheet is half the size of the previous one when folded along its longer side.

83747.subject: Technical Drawing
83747.question_text: Which type of line is used to represent hidden details in an orthographic projection?
83747.explanation: A dashed line (also called a hidden line) is used to show edges or features that are not visible in the current view but exist in the object.

83748.subject: Technical Drawing
83748.question_text: To bisect a given angle using a compass and straightedge, which of the following steps is not required?
83748.explanation: Drawing a line parallel to one of the angle arms is not part of the standard angle bisection procedure. The correct steps involve drawing an arc from the vertex, intersecting the arms, and then drawing arcs from those intersections to find the bisector.

options.text: Draw an arc from the vertex intersecting both arms of the angle
Draw a line parallel to one of the angle arms
Draw arcs from the points where the first arc intersects the angle arms
Draw a line from the vertex through the intersection of the two arcs

83749.subject: Technical Drawing
83749.question_text: Which of the following methods is used to construct a regular pentagon inscribed in a circle?
83749.explanation: The angle division method is used to construct a regular pentagon by dividing the circle into five equal parts of $72^\circ$ each using a protractor or geometric construction.

83750.subject: Technical Drawing
83750.question_text: In first-angle orthographic projection, the right-side view is placed to the left of which view?
83750.explanation: In first-angle projection, the right-side view is placed to the left of the front view. This is a key difference from third-angle projection, where the right-side view is placed to the right of the front view.

83751.subject: Technical Drawing
83751.question_text: Which type of sectional view is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by removing one-quarter of it?
83751.explanation: A half section is used to show the interior details of a symmetrical object by removing one-quarter of it, exposing both the exterior and interior features in a single view.

83752.subject: Technical Drawing
83752.question_text: In isometric drawing, the three principal axes are inclined at what angle to each other?
83752.explanation: In isometric drawing, the three principal axes (length, width, and height) are inclined at $120^\circ$ to each other, creating a 3D representation on a 2D plane.

83753.subject: Technical Drawing
83753.question_text: Which of the following is a correct dimensioning practice in technical drawing?
83753.explanation: Dimensions should be placed outside the outline of the object whenever possible to avoid cluttering the drawing and improve readability.

options.text: Placing dimensions inside the outline of the object
Placing dimensions outside the outline of the object
Using only one arrowhead for each dimension line
Repeating the same dimension in multiple views

83754.subject: Technical Drawing
83754.question_text: Which of the following fasteners is used to prevent relative motion between two parts by fitting into a keyway?
83754.explanation: A key is a machine element used to connect a rotating machine element to a shaft, preventing relative motion between the two parts by fitting into a keyway.
